key_insight: GBClaw links agentic AI-driven atomistic simulations with mechanistic analysis to reveal how grain-boundary defect hierarchies and metastable structures influence sliding resistance.
engineering_relevance: Understanding the structural origins of grain-boundary shear resistance could inform interface engineering in polycrystalline materials.
method: Coordinate LLMs through an orchestrator, specialized agents, domain tools, simulation interfaces, and hierarchical memory.
Use dynamic replanning and iterative workflow refinement to connect systematic simulations with targeted analysis.
Compare boundary sliding with and without secondary misfit dislocations and pursue researcher-guided follow-up calculations.
evidence_signal: Across 14 general asymmetric tilt grain boundaries in nickel, simulations identified diverse deformation modes, substantial defect-dependent shear-strength differences, and anomalously high resistance linked to metastable structures.
watch_item: Evidence is limited to 14 nickel boundaries, and the metastability investigation required researcher-guided follow-up, leaving broader transferability and autonomous mechanistic discovery unestablished.
paper_title: GBClaw: An agentic AI framework for atomistic grain boundary research and mechanistic discovery
